original_card.question: Can a new local cost interface change the deficit-to-recursive-cost ratio beyond current packing?
methods: Propose a changed helper inventory and derive an optimistic exact moment.
Design a small completed instance and independently verify its endpoint and rank bill.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A new physically realizable contract outside the frozen catalogue whose per-call profile, screened with ceiling.ceiling(), beats the selected word's packing ceiling; a lower cap does not establish identical circuitry or order attainable optima, and is insufficient to pass the stronger-budget target under this model.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Packing of the selected word is capped at +0.87% (ceiling model); only a lower local excess spend or a changed coverage law raises the cap.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one changed boundary or helper type with explicit counts.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Mixing only providers already inside the pinned catalogue.

actual_scope: Screen the sixteen open complex kappa claims the queue-ceiling census listed as not covered (CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1104, CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1107, CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1111, CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1117, CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1121, CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1150, CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1154, CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1169, CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1172, CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1175, CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1176, CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1183, CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1192, CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1201, CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1207, CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1218) at their pinned heads, using CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1240's exact relaxation on the per-call local words their packages record.
scope_change_reason: This is the card's 'screen the candidate per-call profile with ceiling.ceiling(); reject routes without headroom' first experiment, applied to the queue claims the census could not cover. It is the second follow-up of the census handoff in discussion 1166, from the reader side; no new inventory is synthesized and no claim is accepted or rejected.
bottleneck_link: The complex side binds. Only a lower local excess spend or a changed coverage law raises a cap; this completes the queue-wide screen (30 of 30 census-listed claims) and shows whether any newly screened word raises the cap.
stop_rule: Screen only what each claim's own package records (documented field aliases and the 896/9 live/calls rule); flag rather than infer anything absent; one bounded pivot maximum.
evidence: RESULT.json: all 16 claims screened (11 distinct local words, 7 new against the census's nine); maximum kappa cap 0.0016872744 (word N1 = census W4), below the census's best cap 0.0016873148; no newly screened word raises the cap; CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1175 is the selected word W2 with a new idle packing; CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1175's PR title kappa differs from its recorded kappa.
author: Aaron Wang / navinor
ai_assistance: Substantial: with help from opencode (task selection, extraction, verify.py and this package).

open_questions.question: Which proposal raises a cap rather than packing toward it?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Only a lower local excess spend or a changed coverage law can move kappa beyond the +0.87% band; the whole census-listed queue is now screened inside it.
open_questions.first_step: Screen each new proposal's per-call profile with ceiling.ceiling() before a full replay, as this package does for the queue.

open_questions.question: Should the uncovered claims record local_profile_per_call and idle_histogram in their result JSONs?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This package had to reach those inputs through field aliases (global_profile, idle_profile, complete_invocations) and, for CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1175, README prose; CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1175's title and recorded kappa also disagree. Structured fields would make the screen mechanical.
open_questions.first_step: Add the two fields plus live/calls to each claim's result JSON, or adopt the census's field names; then rerun research/complex-queue-ceiling-census/rebind.py style checks.
open_questions.blocked_by: The claim authors own their package files; this is a reader-side request only.
